title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page records what is established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. Only a first analysis has been done: the macro rules are not yet known.

Left of the start, the tape is blocks of an odd number of 1s separated by double 0s, and the head reaches the left end in state C; right of the start it is a long stretch of words 1 and 1 1 separated by single 0s, mostly (1 0)^n, which grows like a power of the step count.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in the first 1010 steps (C simulator); the macro configuration and its rules are not yet known, so there is no map to analyse and no heuristic for halting beyond the localisation of the halt below.

Round 6, the proved neighbour. The machine proved in busycoq is this table mirrored and started in state D; in this machine's terms it is the run from the tape 1 A>0 (one extra 1) instead of blank tape. Its proof is a closed tape language that exists once its own run has settled (after 106 steps, not before 105). The same search from this machine's run after 108, 109, 1010 and 1011 steps does not close, so those configurations are not covered by the neighbour's proof. No transfer; the question stays open.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: C with 1 two left, 0 left, 0 under the head. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The proved neighbour is this machine with one extra 1 on the tape
claims.text: From blank tape in state D, three steps lead to state A on blank tape with a single 1 on the cell to its left. busycoq's proved machine 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1LB is this table with left and right exchanged, started in state D (its states A–F are D, E, A, B, C, F here), so its run is this machine's run from 1 A>0. Nothing here says that run and the run from blank tape ever meet.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the tape holds 94,290 ones.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,635 cells have been visited and 19,460 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where a halt can be
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of 5 cells (tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py, closure checked by the script, not by Lean) contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, and its only halting configurations have E reading a 1 with at least four 1s right of the head (E>1 1 1 1 1). In the run so far the right region has shown no runs of five 1s, so a halt would have to happen inside a long block of 1s, as in the left region.

claims.title: Not decided by n-gram CPS up to width 14
claims.text: The n-gram Closed Position Set decider (tools/c/ngramcps.c) with equal widths 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, plain and with the fixed-length (1) and LRU history augmentations, either reaches a halting local configuration (UNKNOWN) or stops at 3·107 local configurations: it does not prove non-halting at these settings.

claims.title: The right end grows by three cells per visit
claims.text: Counting a visit as the head reaching the right end after having been more than 50 cells to its left, the first 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps have 15,470 visits; at 15,386 of them the right end has grown by exactly 3 cells since the previous visit (57 times by 6, the rest by 0, 1 or 5). The head turns back at a point that drifts to the right by about 29 cells per visit, so the zone it sweeps shrinks, and every so often (3,478 times) the turning point jumps far to the left and a new phase starts. Visits get further apart as the right region grows, which gives the power-law growth.

claims.title: The neighbour's proof, reproduced for start D
claims.text: busycoq proves the neighbour with CPS_LRU 100000001 400000 400000 8 3200 2 6 0 0: run 108+1 steps, then find a set of abstract configurations (blocks of 8 cells; on each side the 2 nearest blocks and the list of up to 6 different blocks seen beyond) that is closed under the machine and contains no halt. Our own implementation of that search, on this table started in D, finds such a set with 4,091 abstract configurations from the configuration after 106+1 steps (about 4,035 on busycoq's mirrored machine, also from 107+1 and 108+1). From blank tape and from 105 steps it does not close within 300,000 summaries: the neighbour's run has to settle first. A search program, not a proof.

claims.title: The same search does not close from this machine's run
claims.text: From this machine's own configurations after 108+1 steps (parameters 8,2,6), and after 109+1 and 1010+1 steps with ten parameter sets (blocks of 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 cells; 1 to 8 exact blocks; lists of 4 to 8), and after 1011+1 steps with two, the search either exceeds 300,000 summaries or 6,000,000 abstract configurations, or (blocks of one cell) reaches a halting abstract configuration. A closed set is the smallest one containing its start, so this also shows that these four configurations are not in the neighbour's closed language: had one been, its closure would have stayed inside those 4,091 configurations. It does not show that no closed language exists.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.677).

claims.title: The two regions
claims.text: Left: C>0 1 0^2 1^3 0^2 1^9 0^2 1 0^2 1 0^2 1^357 0^2 ..., blocks of odd length separated by 0^2, a few of them long (one of them has 205, 357 and 421 ones at three of the last left records before 109). Right: words 1 0 and 1 1 0, with long stretches (1 0)^n.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 15, history 1 up to width 14, history 2 up to width 12, history 3 up to width 11, LRU history up to width 4 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 12, p = 3 up to width 12, p = 4 up to width 12, p = 6 up to width 12. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..7; n = 8 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The macro configuration family has not been found, and the proof of the neighbouring start (state D) does not cover this run at any of the four times tested.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: This machine writes blocks of 1s on the left that change like the digits of a counter, and a long stretch of short words on the right that grows like a power of the step count. Its macro rules have not been worked out yet. It has run 10<sup>10</sup> steps without halting.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two regions
html: Left of the start the tape is blocks of an odd number of 1s separated by double 0s, like C>0 1 0^2 1^3 0^2 1^9 0^2 1 0^2 1 0^2 1^357 0^2 1 0^2 1 .... The head arrives at the left end in state C, grows the tape there by one cell, and goes back. Most blocks are short (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) and a few are long, and the long ones grow.

Right of the start the tape is a long stretch of the words 1 0 and 1 1 0, mostly (1 0)^n. It grows like a power of the step count (exponent about 0.68), much faster than the left side, which grows like its logarithm.

sections.heading: Where a halt could happen
html: The machine stops when E reads a 1. A closed tape language with windows of 5 cells, which contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, says more: a halt needs E>1 1 1 1 1, so E must stand on a run of at least five 1s. The right region has not had one in the run so far, so a halt would have to happen in the left region, inside one of its long blocks.

sections.heading: The proved neighbour
html: The community tracker notes that the same table from another start is proved in busycoq. That machine is 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD1LB (verify/CTLv2.v, lemma nonhalt17): this table with left and right exchanged, started in this machine's state D. Lean proves what that start amounts to here: three steps from blank tape in state D give state A with a single 1 on its left. So the proved machine is this one started on 1 A>0 instead of A>0.

The two runs look different. After 108 steps the neighbour's tape is long regular stretches (1 0 0 repeated, and a 22-cell word repeated); this machine's tape still has irregular blocks of 1s (one of 97) and an irregular region of words 1 0 and 1 1 0.

The neighbour's proof is a closed tape language: a finite description of tapes, in blocks of 8 cells, that contains its configuration after 106 steps, is closed under the machine's moves, and contains no halt. We rebuilt the search (c/cpslru.cpp) and it reproduces that result: 4,091 abstract configurations for start D. Started from this machine's own configurations after 108, 109, 1010 and 1011 steps, with the neighbour's parameters and nine others, it never closes. That also tells us these configurations lie outside the neighbour's language, so its theorem says nothing about them.

Two more holdouts are the same table from the remaining starts: 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD (state B, mirrored) and 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC (state C, mirrored). Our search does not close from starts B and C either (after 108 and 109 steps). Of these four starts, only D is proved.

sections.heading: What is not known
html: Not known: the macro configuration (what the head does between visits to the left end), the rules between such configurations, and the map they amount to. The next step is to watch the left end with python3 -m bbtools.explore events and tokenise the right region into the words 1 0 and 1 1 0.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.677).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,635 cells (2,137 left of the start, 32,470 right), with a density of 1s of 0.436.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE1LC: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

family: Counter on the left feeding a growing region on the right (exp/power; structure not yet found)
summary: Left of the start, blocks of odd numbers of 1s separated by 00 change like a counter; right of the start a region of words 1 and 11 grows like a power of the step count; no halt in 10^10 steps; macro rules not yet found. The same table started in state D is proved in busycoq (this machine with one extra 1 on the tape); its closed tape language does not contain this run up to 10^11 steps.
